bibl.title: Lyric for the Rulers, Lyric for the People: The Transformation of Some Lyric Subgenres in Hellenistic Poetry
bibl.seg: 364 Callimachus Carmina varia Graeca Posidippus Pellensis
Silvia Barbantani, Lyric for the Rulers, Lyric for the People: The Transformation of Some Lyric Subgenres in Hellenistic Poetry.
bibl.note: On the reception of some lyric subgenres in Hellenistic poetry. The Alexandrians wrote all types of occasional lyric poetry, a fact that is reflected in Callimachus, Posidippus and Theocritus as well as in the epigrammatic tradition and in poetic fragments on papyri. - 1. Lyric for Rulers and Learned Greeks: 1.1. A new type of encomiastic lyric; - 1.2. Epinikion. Callimachus, Posidippus and inscriptional epigram; - 1.3. Literary epithalamia, threnoi and epikedeia; - 1.4. Poems in stichic lyric meters; - 1.5. Lyric in elegiac epigrams. - 2. Lyric for the People: 2.1. Carmina popularia; - 2.2. Anthologies for symposiastic use; - 2.3. Mimes.
